The client (Edson, an angry reply) says this: "Ownership is mine. It's in the contract and it's registered too. What do you mean I can't take what's mine? I'm going to send a truck to pick it up."

This is an urgent situation: the client intends to remove fiduciarily-pledged essential assets (forklifts, sorting system) from Atlas during the stay period (stay of proceedings) — that's exactly what our strategy says we must not do (Article 49, Paragraph 3 proviso, Article 6, Paragraph 4 and Article 6, Paragraph 7-A; STJ Tema 1.051: removal of essential capital assets during the stay period is prohibited; the RJ (judicial reorganization) court has jurisdiction to order suspension of enforcement and to order return). We need to respond urgently, in plain language, with an explanation of why he must not act unilaterally, the risks (the judge will order return, confrontation with Atlas, jeopardizing the RJ (judicial recovery) claim — he may be ordered to return the goods, it will cause friction, it may damage the negotiation and his claim as a creditor, and may even give Atlas arguments to accuse him of bad faith), and what he can do instead (leverage: negotiation; after the stay period ends, resume enforcement of the guarantee outside the reorganization plan; he's right — ownership is his, his claim is not subordinated to the plan, he will get the goods or payment, just not right now, and not unilaterally).

Deliverables update:
- resposta_cliente.md: add urgent reply section (Round 3).
- estrategia.json: acoes_imediatas (immediate measures) — strengthen item 2 (urgently contact client and prevent removal; if he goes ahead, risk of Article 6, Paragraph 7-A search-and-seizure / return order).
- STATUS.md: add item about client's intent to self-help — open item.
- QUESTIONS.md: maybe add a date/confirmation of whether he actually carried it out.

Contract rules: only authorities from the library; plain language for client replies. Deadline: does removal change deadlines? No — the April 27, 2026 filing stays unchanged; rather, it becomes more urgent to file the objection (divergência), because he wants to formalize his claim as fiduciary creditor.

Legal grounds (library):
- Article 49, Paragraph 3 proviso: "during the suspension period referred to in Article 6, Paragraph 4, it shall not be permitted to sell or remove from the debtor's establishment assets that are essential to its business activity" — the removal prohibition applies regardless of ownership.
- Article 6, Paragraph 7-A: the RJ court has jurisdiction to order suspension of enforcement acts over essential assets for the duration of the stay period (180 days, extendable).
- Tema 1.051 is already indexed as the practical consequence of "essential capital assets" (REsp 1.871.201).
- His ownership is real and protected: Article 49, Paragraph 3 head (main text): his claim is not subordinated to the effects of RJ (judicial reorganization), and ownership rights and contractual conditions prevail — except for the removal proviso. In other words: his right is not being denied; only the timing/method of enforcement is regulated.

Practical risks of self-help removal:
1. The Atlas/RJ administrator can petition the RJ court, and under Article 6, Paragraph 7-A the judge will order suspension/return of the assets — the truck mission will be wasted, and it could be a humiliating public failure.
2. It turns the other side hostile during a critical negotiation (essentiality = his bargaining chip; using force kills the negotiation and makes Atlas seek court protection).
3. It could contaminate his own claim filing and his plan objection (he's the one arguing legality within the RJ framework; unilateral action makes him look bad).
4. It could give Atlas grounds to assert damages. (Carefully: I can't cite Civil Code liability — it's not in the library. Position it not as a legal citation but as a practical risk: "Atlas may seek damages" — label as unverified? Contract rules say anything not in the library must be labeled unverified. I can express it as a practical risk rather than a legal citation: "may lead Atlas to claim damages" — position without citation, and note it as a practical, non-verified risk. Better to leave it as a general practical consequence without pretending to cite law.)
5. The stay period does not run forever — we need to check the processing approval date (deferimento) and set a date for resumption; the moment the stay period ends, he can resume enforcement of the guarantee outside the plan, with no haircut (deságio) (library: practical consequence of lrf_49_essencialidade.md: "at the end of the stay period, enforcement of the guarantee is resumed").

What he can do right now that is powerful:
- File the objection by April 27, 2026 and formally register his creditor status as fiduciary creditor for the full amount of R$900,000.
- Direct negotiation with Atlas: they need the assets; propose payment/renegotiation outside the plan (e.g., Atlas pays in installments and keeps the assets; or a consensual return with substitute collateral — caution: substitute collateral isn't cited; keep it as a practical measure).
- If Atlas is delaying payment / acting in bad faith, file a motion (petition) in the RJ case to set the end date of the stay period / ask the court for... hmm, careful: what can be asked inside the RJ during the stay? The library doesn't include early termination. Don't over-lawyer. Practically: check the approval date and mark the day (Tema: end of stay period → resume).

Tone: firm, respectful, in plain Brazilian Portuguese, urgent — "don't send the truck." Explain in one line: what's being limited is not ownership but the timing of removal (limite não é a propriedade, é o momento da retirada). Use an analogy? Keep it short and direct.

3. STATUS.md — add open item: client's announced intent to remove during the stay period (contained; monitor).

Should I also reply directly in chat? Yes — the user probably wants the reply text to Edson. resposta_cliente.md is the client-facing deliverable; append a new section there, and show the main text in the reply.

Edson-facing draft (plain, respectful, firm):

"Edson, I understand — and on one point you're absolutely right: ownership of the forklifts and the system is yours. That's exactly what the law says (Law 11.101, Article 49, Paragraph 3): your claim does not enter the reorganization plan, ownership rights prevail, and no one is taking anything from you.

The problem is the timing, not ownership. The same law has an explicit proviso: during the stay period (180 days from the RJ's approval), the debtor's essential capital assets cannot be removed from the debtor's establishment — and the Atlas warehouse doesn't work without them (you yourself said so). And the RJ judge has the legal authority (Article 6, Paragraph 7-A) to order — at Atlas's request — the suspension of any act of taking and the immediate return of the assets.

What could actually happen if you send the truck:
1. Atlas calls a lawyer / the administrator, files with the RJ judge, and the judge orders the forklifts returned — the truck goes for nothing and your goods go back anyway;
2. You lose the best bargaining chip you have: right now Atlas is the one who needs you — nothing works without the equipment. With the truck, you turn a negotiation into a confrontation;
3. You weaken your own position in the very procedure you're using to claim your R$2.1 million and oppose the abusive provisions of the plan. Legally no one may take anything from you, but Atlas may try to use your action to claim damages — another problem you don't need.

Your goods will not be lost, and they will not be 'diluted' by the plan. The path that works:
- By April 27: we file your objection registering the R$900,000 as a fiduciary claim outside the plan (this freezes their attempt to apply the 40% haircut);
- We check in the case file the approval date and calculate when the stay ends — from that day on, we resume enforcement of the guarantee outside the plan, without discount, and there the goods leave the warehouse legally;
- In the meantime, we negotiate using the pressure we have: Atlas pays what it owes to keep operating, or we set a date for return with substitute collateral. The one who can't wait is Atlas, not you.

Please do not send the truck. One decision of yours could cost you a negotiation worth R$900,000."

Note the "substitute collateral" — a practical measure, fine. "Atlas may try to claim damages" — label as practical risk (unverified) — I wrote "legally no one may take anything, but Atlas may use your action to claim damages — a risk we haven't verified in our material" — keep as a practical risk with a flag.

- Maybe also add a new first measure "URGENTE (urgent): deactivate the removal order (truck)" — integrate into item 2 to keep it compact.

Also credito_fiduciario.fundamento: add a sentence "The client does not accept the temporary prohibition and announced unilateral removal (20/04) — the prohibition is not a negation of ownership: Article 49, Paragraph 3 head recognizes that the fiduciary claim is not subordinated to RJ (judicial reorganization); only removal of essential assets is suspended during the stay period (Article 6, Paragraph 7-A)." The fundamento is already long; keep the addition short.

Also update the header date/round: "Rodada 3 (Round 3)".

**Edson, por favor, NÃO mande o caminhão.** Ninguém está negando o que é seu — e é justamente aí que está o mal-entendido.

**O senhor tem razão numa coisa, e é a principal:** a propriedade das empilhadeiras e do sistema é de vocês, está no contrato e está registrada. É a própria lei (Lei 11.101, art. 49 §3º) que diz: o crédito do proprietário fiduciário **não entra na recuperação judicial**, e os direitos de propriedade sobre a coisa prevalecem. Ninguém vai "diluir" esses R$ 900 mil no plano da Atlas.

**O que a lei limita não é a propriedade — é o momento e o jeito de retirar.** No mesmo art. 49 §3º há uma ressalva expressa: durante o stay (180 dias contados do deferimento da RJ, prorrogável uma vez), **é proibida a retirada do estabelecimento da devedora dos bens de capital essenciais à sua atividade** — e o senhor mesmo definiu: sem isso, a Atlas para. E o art. 6º §7º-A dá ao juiz da recuperação o poder de mandar suspender qualquer ato de retirada e **determinar a devolução dos bens**, pelo prazo do stay.

**O que acontece na prática se o caminhão aparecer no galpão:**
1. A Atlas (ou o administrador judicial) aciona o juiz da RJ, o juiz manda suspender e **devolver tudo** (art. 6º §7º-A) — o caminhão vai embora de graça e os bens voltam mesmo, só que agora em clima de briga.
2. O senhor **queima a maior alavanca que tem**: hoje quem tem pressa é a Atlas, porque o galpão não funciona sem os equipamentos. Retirada à força transforma negociação em conflito e dá à Atlas motivo para pedir proteção judicial contra vocês.
3. Enfraquece a nossa própria posição nos papéis que estamos protocolando (a divergência de R$ 2,1 mi e a contestação das cláusulas abusivas do plano): nós vamos à Justiça cobrando legalidade, e uma retirada própria jogaria contra nosso discurso. *(Risco prático, a confirmar: a Atlas pode tentar usar o ato para exigir indenização — questão fora do nosso material verificado, mas é dor de cabeça desnecessária.)*

**O caminho que faz o senhor receber — e ele já está montado:**
- **até 27/04:** protocolamos a divergência registrando os R$ 900 mil como **fiduciários, fora do plano** — isso mata qualquer tentativa de aplicar o deságio de 40% que a minuta deles esconde (eles cortariam seus 900 para 540 mil);
- **levantamos nos autos a data do deferimento** e calculamos o dia exato em que o stay acaba: **a partir desse dia, retomamos a execução da garantia fora do plano, sem desconto nenhum** — aí sim os bens saem legalmente, ou o pagamento integral chega;
- **no enquanto, usamos a pressão do jeito certo:** propomos à Atlas pagar/renegociar o contrato fora do plano para manter o galpão rodando. Se eles empurrarem, o senhor espera o fim do stay com o crédito preservado — a paciência, aqui, é o que mais dói neles.

Resumindo: **a propriedade é sua, o bloqueio é temporário (180 dias, prorrogáveis) e a estratégia já garante o seu retorno — com o valor cheio.** Mandar o caminhão hoje custa dinheiro; esperar até o fim do stay e negociar com essa arma na mão é o caminho dos R$ 900 mil inteiros.

## Resposta ao Edson (enviada em `resposta_cliente.md`, seção URGENTE)

**Não mande o caminhão.** E o argumento dele está certo pela metade — é aí que mora o perigo:

- **Ele tem razão no essencial:** a propriedade é dele, e é a própria lei (LRF art. 49 §3º, regra) que diz que o crédito do proprietário fiduciário **não entra na recuperação judicial** e os direitos de propriedade prevalecem. Ninguém vai cortar seus R$ 900 mil — a cláusula de "deságio de 40%" para fiduciários não o vincula.
- **O que a lei limita não é a propriedade, é o momento da retirada:** a ressalva do próprio art. 49 §3º veda, durante o stay (180 dias do deferimento, prorrogável), a retirada do estabelecimento da devedora de **bens de capital essenciais** — e ele mesmo disse que sem isso a Atlas para. O art. 6º §7º-A dá ao juiz da RJ poder para mandar suspender o ato e **devolver os bens**.
- **Consequências práticas do caminhão:** (1) Atlas/AJ aciona o juízo → ordem de devolução, o caminhão volta de graça; (2) queima a alavanca — quem tem pressa é a Atlas, o galpão não funciona sem os equipamentos; (3) contamina nossa posição na divergência de R$ 2,1 mi e na objeção às cláusulas ilegais do plano. *(Apossível pedido de indenização pela Atlas: risco prático sinalizado, fora do material verificado.)*
- **O caminho que entrega o dinheiro:** divergência protocolada até 27/04 travando o deságio; data do deferimento levantada nos autos para marcar o dia exato do fim do stay — **aí a execução da garantia retoma fora do plano, sem desconto**; e no intervalo, negociação direta com a Atlas pagando para manter o galpão rodando.
